The fluid-mosaic model of the plasma membrane (Singer and Nicolson, 1972) -- a fluid phospholipid bilayer in which proteins float like icebergs.
Mitochondrion and chloroplast in section. Both are double-membraned and semi-autonomous, with their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.

Mitosis in a cell with $2n = 4$, followed by cytokinesis. Sister chromatids separate at anaphase, so each daughter cell is again diploid.
Meiosis in a cell with $2n = 4$. Homologues cross over in prophase I and separate at anaphase I; sister chromatids separate only at anaphase II, giving four haploid cells.

*Pinus*: a long shoot bearing dwarf shoots with fascicles of needles, the male and female cones, and a winged seed lying naked on a cone scale.

Monocotyledon and dicotyledon compared through the seed, leaf venation, root system and a transverse section of the stem.

Transverse section of a dicot stem (stained, low power): the vascular bundles lie in a ring around a central pith.
Floral diagrams of the four prescribed families. The dot at the top of each is the position of the mother axis; brackets in the formulae mean fused members.
Basic shapes of bacteria (top row) and the arrangements produced when daughter cells stay together after binary fission.

Spherical bacteria (cocci) of *Staphylococcus*, in the irregular grape-like clusters that give the genus its name, seen in a stained smear.
Ultrastructure of a rod-shaped bacterium. Compare it with the eukaryotic cell of Unit 1: there is no nuclear envelope and no membrane-bound organelle of any kind.

The two wall patterns revealed by Gram's stain, drawn in section with the outside of the cell upwards. The Gram-negative wall has little peptidoglycan but adds an outer membrane of lipopolysaccharide.
A real Gram-stained smear of mixed bacteria: Gram-positive cells keep the crystal violet and appear purple, Gram-negative cells lose it and take the pink counterstain.
Structure of the T4 bacteriophage (a tailed DNA virus of *E. coli*) and of tobacco mosaic virus (a helical RNA virus). Sizes are approximate.
Electron micrograph of a T4 bacteriophage: the angular head holds the DNA, and a rigid tail ends in a base plate and thin tail fibres.
Tobacco mosaic virus particles (negative-stain TEM): stiff straight rods, each a helix of protein around a single RNA strand. Scale bar 0.2 μm.

Unidirectional flow of energy through a grassland ecosystem, in kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹. At every step about 90 % of the energy is lost, which is Lindeman's ten per cent law.
The three ecological pyramids. Pyramids of number and of biomass may be inverted; the pyramid of energy is always upright, because energy can only be lost upwards.
The nitrogen cycle. Nitrogen gas is useless to plants until it is fixed; it returns to the air only by denitrification. The bacteria responsible for each step are named.
The carbon cycle. Photosynthesis is the only large route into the living world; respiration, decomposition and the combustion of fossil fuels are the routes out.
Hydrosere — the six seral stages by which an oxbow lake of the Terai silts up and becomes forest. Each community makes the site less suitable for itself and more suitable for the next.

Classification of software. System software runs the machine; application software does the user's work. Web-based and mobile applications are simply application software delivered in a different way.
The layered view of a computer system. Each layer speaks only to its immediate neighbours, so a word processor never touches the disk controller directly — it asks the operating system.
The main functions of an operating system. The kernel is the part of the OS that is always resident in memory and performs these functions.

Parts of an application window. Every Windows program uses the same furniture, which is why a user who knows one program can find their way around another.
A small part of a Windows folder tree. The full name of a file is its path: the drive, then every folder from the root, then the file name and extension.
Layered architecture of a Linux system. Only the kernel talks to the hardware; the shell is the command interpreter between the user and the kernel.
Share of the worldwide smartphone operating system market, approximate figures for 2025. Android leads globally, while iOS has a much larger share in high-income markets than in South Asia.
Classification of application packages. The office package is general purpose and is used by everybody; domain-specific tools are written for one line of business.
A word-processed page with the features that carry marks: margins, header and footer, heading style, justified paragraph, bulleted list, table and automatic page number.
Parts of a spreadsheet window. The name box shows the address of the active cell and the formula bar shows what was actually typed into it, not the displayed result.
A chart drawn from a range of spreadsheet cells. If a mark in the worksheet is changed, the chart redraws itself immediately.
Presentation software. The normal view shows one slide with its placeholders and the speaker notes; the slide sorter view shows the whole deck so that slides can be reordered.

A school management system. Every module reads from and writes to one shared database, which is why a fee paid at the counter is visible instantly in the student's record.
Levels of programming language. The higher you go, the closer the language is to human thought and the further it is from the hardware; the more translation is then needed before the CPU can run it.

The parts of a C program. Only main() is compulsory; everything above it prepares the compiler and everything below it is the work broken into functions.
Functions in C are either supplied with the compiler (library) or written by the programmer (user-defined).
How a function call works. Control leaves main(), the arguments are copied into the parameters, the body runs, and return sends one value back to exactly the point of the call.

चित्लाङको डाँडाबाट देखिने पहाडी बाटो र बस्ती — कथामा यात्रीले 'आज चित्लाङ पुग्ने विचार' गरेको ठाउँको परिवेश
निबन्धको केन्द्रीय रूपक — नेपाल बार्दलीसहितको पाँच तले घर। दायाँतिर पाठमै उल्लिखित उचाइअनुसारका जलवायु कटिबन्ध।
पाठको दोस्रो अनुच्छेदमा वर्णित वनको आहार सञ्जाल। सूर्यबाट सुरु भई माटोमा फर्कने चक्र।
चितवन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जको हात्ती सफारी — पाठमा उल्लिखित पर्यापर्यटनको प्रत्यक्ष उदाहरण।
बिहानको समाचारपत्र पढिरहेका एक जना — नाटकको 'ताजा खबर', पत्रिका र पोस्टर-पम्प्लेटको परिवेश सम्झाउने दृश्य
लघु नाटकको मञ्चसज्जा र प्रवेश–निकास (रङ्गसङ्केतअनुसार)
घटनाक्रम — कथानकका चार चरण
सुन्दर छन्त्यालको विफलताबाट सफलतासम्मको यात्रा
रिपोर्ताजको स्थान र यसका आधारभूत तत्त्व
संवादात्मक रचनाको संरचना — नाटकसँगको तुलनामा
बद्रीको कृषिशालाका इकाइ र तिनले सिकाउने प्रविधि
नेपालमा धान रोपाइँ — कृषिकर्म मानव जातिको अस्तित्वसँग जोडिएको आधारभूत काम हो
रारा जाने मार्गचित्र — दैनिकीले नै नाम लिएका पडावहरू (सङ्केतात्मक रेखाचित्र, वास्तविक नक्सा होइन)
रारा ताल — चारैतिर सदाबहार वनस्पतिले भरिएका डाँडाले घेरिएको नेपालकै सबैभन्दा ठुलो ताल
दैनिकीको ढाँचा — परीक्षामा एक दिनको दैनिकी लेख्ने पाँच पत्रे खाका
जलविद्युत् आयोजनाका तीन प्रकार — पानी सञ्चय गर्ने क्षमताअनुसारको वर्गीकरण
कुलेखानी — नेपालको जलाशययुक्त जलविद्युत् आयोजना; बाँधले थुनेपछि बनेको इन्द्रसरोवर र त्यसको जलाधार
वक्तृताको संरचना — परीक्षामा जस्ताको तस्तै प्रयोग गर्न मिल्ने छ चरण
मुखको काटछाँट चित्र — व्यञ्जनका पाँच मुख्य उच्चारण स्थान, पछाडिबाट अगाडितिर।
नेपाली वर्णको वर्गीकरण वृक्ष। कोष्ठकभित्रको अङ्कले लेख्य वर्णको सङ्ख्या जनाउँछ।
शब्दको दुई ढङ्गको वर्गीकरण — बायाँ बनोटका आधारमा, दायाँ स्रोतका आधारमा।
शब्दकोशीय वर्णक्रम मिलाउने तीन चरण — क-बाट सुरु हुने छ शब्दको क्रम।
नेपाली पदवर्गको वर्गीकरण। विकारी पदले रूप फेर्छन्, अविकारीले फेर्दैनन्।
क्रियापदको वर्गीकरण — कर्मका आधारमा, बनोटका आधारमा र प्रयोगका आधारमा।
पाँच अविकारी पदवर्ग — प्रत्येकले वाक्यमा गर्ने काम।
एउटै सर्वनाम *म* विभक्तिअनुसार कसरी रूप फेर्छ — रूपायनको नमुना।
वाक्य टुङ्ग्याउने चिह्न छान्ने निर्णय वृक्ष।
इकार र उकार ह्रस्व लेख्ने कि दीर्घ — निर्णय वृक्ष।
पदयोग गर्ने कि पदवियोग — निर्णय वृक्ष।
शब्दनिर्माणका चार प्रक्रिया — यो एकाइ पहिलोको हो।
एउटै मूल शब्द *मान* मा फरक उपसर्ग लाग्दा अर्थ कसरी फेरिन्छ।
प्रत्ययका दुई वर्ग — आधार शब्द के हो, त्यसैले वर्ग तय हुन्छ।
कुनै प्रत्यय कृत् हो कि तद्धित — छुट्याउने निर्णय-बाटो।
कुन पद प्रधान छ — यसैले समासको भेद तय हुन्छ।
समासको भेद छुट्याउने निर्णय-बाटो — माथिबाट क्रमशः सोध्दै जानुहोस्।
द्वित्वका तीन भेद र प्रत्येकको नमुना।
सन्धिका तीन भेद; स्वर सन्धिका पाँच उपभेद नमुनासहित।
उद्देश्य र विधेय अनि तिनका विस्तार — एउटै वाक्यमा देखाइएको।
कर्तृवाच्यबाट कर्मवाच्य बनाउने चार चरण।
पठनबोध सुल्झाउने पाँच चरण। तेस्रो चरणमा मात्र लेख्न थालिन्छ — त्यसअघिका दुई चरण पढाइका हुन्।
लेखन सिप खण्डका छ प्रश्नमा अङ्क र सुझाइएको समय। कुल ३६ अङ्कका लागि करिब ९५ मिनेट छुट्याउनुहोस्, बाँकी समय व्याकरण र पाठगत प्रश्नलाई।
निबन्धको तीन भाग र ४०० शब्दमा तिनको अनुमानित हिस्सा। विषय विस्तारमै निबन्धको तीन-चौथाइ भाग हुनुपर्छ।
स्वतन्त्र रचनाका २५ मिनेट कसरी बाँड्ने। पहिलो पाँच मिनेट खाकामा लगानी गर्दा बाँकी बीस मिनेट रोकिनु पर्दैन।
निवेदनको ढाँचा — आठ भागको कङ्काल। परीक्षामा यी आठै भाग देखिनुपर्छ।
गोरखापत्रको एक पुरानो अङ्क। सार्वजनिक सूचना, विज्ञापन र नियमावली एउटै पृष्ठमा राखिने परम्परागत ढाँचा यहाँ देख्न सकिन्छ।
टिप्पणी र प्रतिवेदनको तुलना — दुवै औपचारिक, तर कार्यचक्रमा फरक ठाउँमा उभिन्छन्।
नेपाली शब्दभण्डारका स्रोत। आगन्तुक वर्गभित्रका उपवर्ग परीक्षामा छुट्टै सोधिन्छन्।
उखान र टुक्काको तुलना। परीक्षामा 'यी दुईबिचको भिन्नता लेख्नुहोस्' भनी सोधिन्छ।
गोपालप्रसाद रिमाल — नेपाली गद्य कविताका आरम्भकर्ता।
कविताको संवाद-त्रिकोण। आमाले सपना बोकेकी छन्, छोराले प्रश्न सोध्छ र 'त्यो' अर्थात् क्रान्ति हुरीझैँ आउँछ।
जङ्गलमा एक्ली बसेकी दमयन्ती — राजा रवि वर्माको चित्रकला (सार्वजनिक स्वामित्वको कृति)।
दमयन्तीको यात्राक्रम। चरण १ बाट ६ सम्म घटनाको क्रम सम्झन यस चित्रलाई प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्।
तारानाथ शर्मा — नियात्रा विधाका स्थापक र झर्रोवादी आन्दोलनका अगुवा।
बैतडी जिल्लाको पाटन क्षेत्रको एउटा दृश्य — पाठको यात्रा यही भेगको उकाला-ओरालो हुँदै अघि बढ्छ।
पाठको यात्रा-क्रम। पाटन र अघोरी गाडको भाग तेर्सो बाटो हो भने घनघस्याको उकालो सबैभन्दा कठिन खण्ड हो।
औपचारिक व्यावसायिक पत्रको ढाँचा। माथिबाट तलतिर पत्रशीर्ष, मिति, प्रापक, विषय, व्यहोरा र हस्ताक्षर मिलाउनुहोस्।
धानको रोपाइँ — उपन्यासको परिवारको जीविका र खुसीको केन्द्र; अष्टनारानका लागि रोपाइँको दिन सबैभन्दा ठुलो पर्व थियो।
उपन्यासको कथावस्तुका पाँच चरण। सुरु र अन्त्य दुवै मृत्युमा टुङ्गिएको छ — पहिलो एक किसानको, अन्तिम सिङ्गो परिवारको।
उपन्यासका मुख्य पात्रको सम्बन्ध। बायाँ अष्टनारानको किसान परिवार, दायाँ शोषक पात्र; तीर नानीथकुँतिर जाल फैलाउने प्रयास देखाउँछ।
स्टिफन हकिङ (सन् २००८ मा एक व्याख्यानको बेला) — ह्विलचेयरमा जडान गरिएको कम्प्युटरको सहायताले उनी आफ्ना विचार व्यक्त गर्थे।
हकिङको जीवनका मुख्य वर्ष। रोगले अङ्ग-अङ्ग शिथिल बनाउँदै गए पनि अनुसन्धानको बाटो रोकिएन।
हकिङका तीन शक्ति र तिनको सम्मिलित परिणाम।
चोला उपत्यकाबाट देखिएको आमा दब्लम शिखर — हिमचुलीले जसरी बोलाउँछन् भनेर कविले लेखेका छन्, त्यही दृश्य।
कविताको यात्रा — उकालीदेखि हिमचुलीसम्म। प्रत्येक तहमा कविताले चित्रण गरेको स्थान र जीवन।
डाँफे (हिमाली मुनाल) — नेपालको राष्ट्रिय पन्छी। कविताले यसलाई 'नौरङ्गे डाँफे' भनी हिमालको प्रतीक बनाएको छ।
गजलको संरचना — पाठ्यपुस्तककै 'सुनेकै हो मैले' गजलको मत्ला र मक्ता। रदिफ र काफियाको स्थान देखाइएको छ।
नेपाली आमा र बच्चाको स्नेहिल तस्बिर (कथाकी पात्र होइन) — 'मेरा छोराछोरी मेरा लागि चन्द्र र सूर्य हुन्' भन्ने ममताको भावको प्रतीक।
कथाका पात्रबिचको सम्बन्ध — ममता केन्द्रमा छे; सुबोधसँगको सम्बन्ध आशाबाट घृणातिर र सन्तानसँगको सम्बन्ध सधैँ अटल रहन्छ।
ममताको मनको उतारचढाव — घटनाका खण्डअनुसार गुणात्मक रेखाचित्र (सङ्ख्यात्मक मान होइन)।
खुकुरी — गोर्खाली बहादुरीको प्रतीक। कथाको 'गोर्खे' नामले यही पहिचान सम्झाउँछ, तर प्रस्तुत भने कम्प्युटरभित्रको योद्धाको।
कथाको घटनाक्रम — पेशलको सिर्जनादेखि कम्प्युटर मर्मतसम्म (कालक्रमअनुसार)।
कथाका दुई संसार — बाहिरी संसारका मानिस र कम्प्युटरभित्रको संसारका पात्र, जसलाई पेशलको आदेश (स्क्यान, अपडेट) ले जोड्छ।
काठमाडौँको टुँडिखेलमा आयोजित उधौली-साकेला उत्सवमा राई समुदायका महिला — नेपालको जातीय-सांस्कृतिक विविधताको एउटा झलक।
काठमाडौँ दरबार क्षेत्रमा इन्द्रजात्राको रथयात्रा — नेवार समुदायको पर्व, जसमा विभिन्न समुदायका हजारौँ मानिस सहभागी हुन्छन्।
छलफलको तर्कक्रम — प्रश्न उठानदेखि निष्कर्षसम्म। प्रत्येक चरणमा बोल्ने पात्र कोष्ठकमा।
रोबर्ट ओवेन (सन् १७७१–१८५८) को उठेको मूर्तिकला (बासरिलिफ) को तस्बिर — पाठमा 'आधुनिक सहकारीका पिता' भनिएका बेलायती विद्वान्।
सहकारीको यात्रा — विश्व र नेपालको समयरेखा। माथि विश्वका घटना (सन्), तल नेपालका घटना (वि.सं.)।
अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सहकारी महासङ्घका सात निर्देशक सिद्धान्त (पाठअनुसार)।
सगरमाथा (चोमोलुङ्मा), नुप्से र खुम्बु हिमनदी। पाठको औद्योगिक प्रतिष्ठानको नाम संसारको सर्वोच्च शिखरकै अर्को नामबाट राखिएको हो।
बाँसको डोको — पहाडका भरियाले नाम्लोको सहायताले बोक्ने परम्परागत बाँसका भाँडा। छिरिङका बुबा यस्तै भारी बोक्ने काम गर्थे।
लेखकको यात्रा — कोटेश्वरदेखि सोलुसल्लेरीसम्म (पाठमा उल्लिखित ठाउँ)।
अक्षरका तीन अङ्ग। शिखरमा स्वर अनिवार्य छ; आरम्भ र अन्त्य खाली रहन सक्छन्।
अक्षरीकरणको चार चरण — शब्द *नमस्कार* मा लागू गरेर देखाइएको।
एउटै शब्दको वर्ग ऊ कुन पदलाई खुलाउँछ त्यसमा भर पर्छ। माथिको चापले कुन पदलाई खुलाएको हो सो देखाउँछ।
कुनै रेखाङ्कित पदको वर्ग छुट्याउने निर्णय-बाटो। माथिबाट क्रमशः सोध्दै जानुहोस्; उत्तर \"हो\" आएकै ठाउँमा रोकिनुहोस्।
आदरका चार तह। तल्लोबाट माथिल्लोतिर जाँदा सर्वनाम र क्रिया दुवैको रूप सँगै फेरिन्छ।
सङ्गति मिलाउने क्रम — कर्ता हेरेर चारै कोटि तय गरेपछि क्रियाको रूप आफैँ निस्कन्छ।
वाक्यको दुई आधारबाट वर्गीकरण। संरचनाका तीन र अर्थका आठ भेद परीक्षामा सोधिन्छन्।
एउटै कुरा तीनै संरचनामा। जोड्ने शब्द फेरिँदा संरचना फेरिन्छ, अर्थ उही रहन्छ।
धातु 'गर्-' को बाह्र काल-पक्ष रूप। तीन कालले तीन स्तम्भ, चार पक्षले चार हरफ बनाउँछन्।
अनुनासिक लेख्ने निर्णय। पछिको वर्ण कुन हो, त्यसैले पञ्चम वर्ण कि शिरबिन्दु तय गर्छ।
पाँच भाव र तिनका क्रियाचिनो। चिनो देखेपछि भाव तय गर्न सकिन्छ।
सङ्केतार्थका दुई किसिम। सर्त अझै सम्भव छ कि छैन — त्यसैले क्रियारूप तय हुन्छ।
शब्दनिर्माणको संरचना। मूल बिचमा रहन्छ; अगाडि उपसर्ग, पछाडि प्रत्यय जोडिन्छन्।
मोतीराम भट्टको मत्लामा काफिया र रदीफ। काफिया तुक मिलाउँछ, रदीफ जस्ताको तस्तै दोहोरिन्छ।
द्वित्वका चार किसिम। दोस्रो पद पहिलोसँग कति मिल्छ, त्यसैले किसिम तय हुन्छ।
समासको वर्गीकरण। विग्रह गरेपछि कुन पद प्रधान छ भनी हेर्दा भेद आफैँ निस्कन्छ।
आठ कारक, तिनका प्रश्न र विभक्ति चिह्न। क्रियालाई प्रश्न सोध्दा कारक आफैँ निस्कन्छ।
तीन दोहोरो विभक्ति। चिनो उही भए पनि क्रियासँगको सम्बन्ध फरक हुन्छ।
संश्लेषण — तीन सरल वाक्य एउटै वाक्यमा। दोहोरिएको कर्ता हट्छ, बाँकी विशेषण बन्छन्।
एउटै वाक्यको तीन वाच्य। कर्ताको विभक्ति, कर्मको ठाउँ र क्रियाको रूप — तीनै सँगै फेरिन्छन्।
नेपालीको आधारभूत पदक्रम। हरेक विशेषक आफ्नो विशेष्यभन्दा अघि, क्रिया सबैभन्दा पछाडि।
अल्पविराम एक पद सर्दा अर्थ ठिक उल्टो हुन्छ — चिह्न सजावट होइन, अर्थ हो।
उक्ति परिवर्तनको सीढी — तलबाट माथि, क्रमै मिलाएर। एउटा खुड्किलो छुट्यो भने वाक्य बिग्रिन्छ।
शब्दकोशीय प्रविष्टिका अङ्ग। शीर्ष शब्दपछिका संक्षेपले कोटि र स्रोत भाषा जनाउँछन्।
पठनबोधका छ चरण। दोस्रो पढाइमा चिनो लगाउने चरण नछुटाउनुहोस् — त्यही चरणले उत्तर कहाँ छ भन्ने नक्सा बनाइदिन्छ।
पठनबोधको सबैभन्दा सस्तो अभ्यास दैनिक पत्रिका हो। समाचारले तथ्यबोध, सम्पादकीयले आशयबोध र विचार स्तम्भले मूल्याङ्कन गर्ने बानी बसाल्छ।
बुँदाटिपोटको मानक ढाँचा। उपबुँदा एक तह मात्र गहिरो जानुहोस् — दोस्रो तहको उपबुँदा राख्दा यो टिपोट होइन, नक्कल बन्छ।
सारांश लेखनको पाँच पाइले प्रक्रिया र लम्बाइको हिसाब। ४५० शब्दको गद्यांशको सारांश करिब १५० शब्दको हुनुपर्छ।
निबन्धको चार अङ्ग र आठ अङ्कको अनुमानित बाँडफाँट। विषय विस्तारले आधाभन्दा बढी ठाउँ र आधा अङ्क ओगट्छ — यही भाग छोट्याउँदा निबन्ध कमजोर हुन्छ।
एउटा अनुच्छेदको चार अङ्ग। विषयवाक्यले दाबी गर्छ, विस्तारले खोल्छ, प्रमाणले पुष्टि गर्छ, जोडवाक्यले अर्को अनुच्छेदतिर लैजान्छ।
निबन्धका चालीस मिनेटको बाँडफाँट। पाँच मिनेटको खाकाले लेखाइको बाँकी पैँतिस मिनेट जोगाउँछ।
प्रतिक्रिया लेखनको चार खण्डे ढाँचा र चार अङ्कको बाँडफाँट। पहिलो खण्ड छोटो राख्नुहोस् — सारांश लामो भयो भने प्रतिक्रियाको ठाउँ नै रहँदैन।
निवेदनको मानक ढाँचा। निवेदनमा मिति सबैभन्दा माथि दायाँ, विषय त्यसपछि, अनि मात्र सम्बोधन आउँछ — यही क्रम कार्यालय पत्रमा उल्टिन्छ।
कार्यालय पत्रको ढाँचा। निवेदनको ठिक उल्टो — यहाँ विषय बिचमा र सम्बोधनभन्दा माथि आउँछ, अनि पत्र संख्या बायाँ र मिति दायाँ राखिन्छ।
सुनकोशी गाउँपालिकाको वडा कार्यालय, थुम्पाखर, सिन्धुपाल्चोक। सरकारी नामपाटीको क्रम आफैँमा एउटा ढाँचा हो — माथि निशान छाप, अनि तह, अनि कार्यालयको नाम, अनि ठेगाना।
टिप्पणीको यात्रा। निर्णय लेखिएपछि टिप्पणी 'टिप्पणी आदेश' बन्छ, निर्णय किताबमा चढ्छ र बाहिर जाँदा पत्रको रूप लिन्छ।
प्रतिवेदनको तीन भाग र नौ खण्ड। मूल भागमा तथ्य मात्र राख्ने; आफ्नो राय सुझाव खण्डमा मात्र लेख्ने — यही अनुशासनले प्रतिवेदनलाई निबन्धबाट छुट्याउँछ।
सिंहदरबारको मूल ढोका, काठमाडौँ। कार्यालय पत्रको शिरपानामा लेखिने 'सिंहदरबार, काठमाडौँ' भन्ने ठेगाना यही परिसरको हो।
शब्दभण्डारको नक्सा — कक्षा १२ को पाठ्यक्रममा सोधिने शब्दका आठ प्रकार र प्रत्येकको एक उदाहरण।
उखान र टुक्काको तुलना — परीक्षामा 'यी दुईबिचको भिन्नता लेख्नुहोस्' भनी सोध्न सकिन्छ।
Accuracy is closeness to the true value (the bullseye); precision is closeness of the readings to each other. They are independent.
Vernier callipers. Ten vernier divisions span nine millimetres, so the least count is 0.1 mm. Here the vernier zero lies past 13 mm and its 4th division coincides, giving 13 + 4(0.1) = 13.4 mm.
A vernier calliper. The jaws on the left grip the object; the sliding vernier scale beside the fixed main scale gives the fractional millimetre.
A micrometer screw gauge. The object is held between the anvil and the spindle; the thimble (circular scale) is turned until the ratchet clicks.
Testing the dimensional prediction $T \propto \sqrt{l}$ for a simple pendulum. The $T^2$ against $l$ graph is a straight line through the origin of slope $4\pi^2/g$.
Parallelogram law. $OC$ is the resultant of $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$; the perpendicular $CD$ dropped on $OA$ produced supplies the derivation.
Polygon law: four vectors drawn head to tail, with the closing side (red) as the resultant. If the last head met the first tail, the resultant would be zero.
Rectangular resolution. $A_x = A\cos\theta$ and $A_y = A\sin\theta$ are the sides of the right triangle whose hypotenuse is $\vec{A}$.
The magnitude of $\vec{A}\times\vec{B}$ equals the area of the parallelogram they span, base $A$ times height $B\sin\theta$. The product vector points out of the page.
As $\Delta t$ shrinks, the chord PQ rotates into the tangent at P. The slope of the tangent is the instantaneous velocity.
Relative velocity of A with respect to B is the vector $\vec{v}_A + (-\vec{v}_B)$.
Velocity–time graph for uniform acceleration. The slope gives $a$; the shaded area gives the displacement $s$.
Trajectories for a fixed speed at several angles. Complementary angles ($30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$) give the same range; $45^\circ$ gives the maximum.
Force-time graph for a collision lasting 10 ms. The shaded area is the impulse; the dashed line is the constant average force that would deliver the same impulse.
Head-on collision. Whatever happens during contact, the total momentum $m_1u_1 + m_2u_2$ before equals $m_1v_1 + m_2v_2$ after.
Atwood machine. Isolating each mass gives $m_1g - T = m_1a$ and $T - m_2g = m_2a$.
Principle of moments. The beam balances when $W_1d_1 = W_2d_2$; the pivot supplies the upward reaction $R$.
Friction against applied force. Static friction grows to match the applied force up to the limiting value, then drops to the smaller, roughly constant kinetic friction.
A block on the point of sliding down a rough plane. Along the slope $mg\sin\theta = f = \mu_s mg\cos\theta$, so $\mu_s = \tan\theta$.
Only the component $F\cos\theta$ along the displacement does work. The vertical component $F\sin\theta$ reduces the normal reaction but does no work.
Work done is the area under the $F$–$x$ graph. For a spring $F = kx$, so the area from $0$ to $x$ is the triangle $\frac{1}{2}kx^2$.
Energy of a body falling freely from height $H$. $U$ falls linearly, $K$ rises linearly, and the total $K+U = mgH$ stays constant.
Head-on elastic collision of a $2$ kg body at $6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ with a stationary $4$ kg body. The lighter body rebounds; momentum and kinetic energy both balance.
Angular displacement $\theta = s/r$. The direction of $\vec{\omega}$ is given by the right-hand rule, along the axis of rotation.

Load–extension graph. The straight part obeys Hooke's law and its slope is the force constant $k$. Past the elastic limit the graph curves and the body no longer returns to its original length.
Stress–strain curve for a ductile metal such as mild steel. $P$ is the proportional limit, $E$ the elastic limit, $Y$ the yield point, $U$ the ultimate tensile stress and $B$ the breaking point.
The three deformations. (a) tensile stress changes length, (b) hydraulic stress changes volume, (c) tangential stress changes shape through the angle $\theta$.

A hot body and a cold body in thermal contact. Energy flows until both reach the same temperature; after that the net flow is zero, though molecular collisions continue.
Zeroth law. $A$ and $B$ are separated by an insulating wall but each is in contact with $C$ through a conducting wall. If $T_A = T_C$ and $T_B = T_C$, then $T_A = T_B$.
Mercury-in-glass thermometer. The length of the thread measured from the bulb is $l_0$ at the ice point, $l_{100}$ at the steam point and $l_t$ at the unknown temperature $t$.
Pullinger's apparatus. The rod expands inside a steam jacket and the expansion is read on a micrometer screw whose contact with the rod completes the bell circuit.
A square of side $l$ heated through $\Delta\theta$. The two shaded strips have total area $2l\,\delta l$; the corner square $(\delta l)^2$ is far smaller and is neglected, giving $\beta = 2\alpha$.
Anomalous expansion of water. Between $0\ ^\circ$C and $4\ ^\circ$C water contracts on heating, so its density is greatest at $4\ ^\circ$C.
Dulong and Petit's apparatus. The two limbs of liquid balance at the base, so $h_0\rho_0 = h_\theta\rho_\theta$ and the expansion of the glass never enters the result.
Left: a body at $80^\circ$C cooling in surroundings at $20^\circ$C. Right: the same data plotted as $\ln(\theta-\theta_0)$ against $t$ gives a straight line of slope $-k$.
Calorimeter for the method of mixtures. Lagging and the polished outer vessel cut down heat exchange with the room.
Heating curve for 1 kg of water substance from $-20^\circ$C ice to $120^\circ$C steam. The temperature stands still while a phase change is in progress.
Phase diagram of water (pressure on a logarithmic scale). The fusion curve leans backwards, so extra pressure lowers the melting point of ice.
Steady conduction through a slab. In the steady state the temperature falls uniformly from $\theta_1$ to $\theta_2$ across the thickness $L$.
Searle's apparatus. The heat conducted between the two thermometers in the bar is collected by the flowing water.
Daytime valley wind. The sunlit slope heats the air against it, which rises, and cooler air flows up the valley to replace it.
Black-body spectra at three temperatures. As $T$ rises the peak grows, the total area grows much faster, and $\lambda_m$ moves to shorter wavelengths.
Left: Boyle's law isotherms for one mole. Right: Charles's law. Every line, extrapolated back, meets the temperature axis at $-273.15\ ^\circ$C.
Force between two molecules. It is strongly repulsive when they are pushed closer than $r_0$ and weakly attractive beyond it.
A molecule of mass $m$ rebounding elastically from the shaded face of a cube of side $l$. Only the $x$-component of its velocity is reversed.
Maxwell distribution of molecular speeds for oxygen. Raising the temperature flattens and broadens the curve and shifts it to higher speeds.
Terms used for spherical mirrors. For a concave mirror $F$ and $C$ lie in front of the mirror; for a convex mirror they lie behind it and are only virtual points.
Concave mirror with the object beyond $C$. The three reflected rays actually cross in front of the mirror, so the image is real, inverted and diminished.
Convex mirror. The reflected rays diverge; only their backward extensions (dashed) meet, behind the mirror, so the image is virtual, erect and diminished.
Geometry for the mirror formula. The two shaded triangles about the pole are similar; so are the triangles that meet at $F$, because $MP \\approx AB$ for paraxial rays.

Refraction at a plane boundary. Going into the denser medium the ray bends towards the normal; coming out of it the ray bends away from the normal. The faint grey ray is the partially reflected light.
Real and apparent depth. Rays from the coin at $O$ bend away from the normal as they leave the water, so to the eye above they seem to come from the shallower point $I$.
A ray through a parallel-sided slab of thickness $t$. The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but displaced sideways by the lateral shift $d$.
Total internal reflection. As $i$ grows the refracted ray bends further from the normal; at $i = C$ it grazes the surface, and for $i > C$ no light escapes at all.
Refraction through a prism of refracting angle $A$. The ray is refracted at $Q$ and again at $S$, and leaves deviated through the angle $\delta$ from its original direction.
Deviation against angle of incidence for an equilateral prism with $n = 1.5$. Any deviation above the minimum is produced by two different angles of incidence; at the minimum the two coincide.
At minimum deviation the path is symmetrical about the bisector of the refracting angle, and the internal ray runs parallel to the base.
A thin prism of refracting angle $A = 20^{\circ}$. The emergent ray is turned through $\delta \approx (n-1)A$ from the incident direction, almost independently of how the ray enters.
The six common thin lenses. A lens thicker at the centre than at the rim converges light; one thinner at the centre diverges it.
Convex lens with the object beyond $2F_1$. The three standard rays meet at the image, which is real, inverted and diminished.
Concave lens. The emergent rays diverge; their backward extensions (dashed) meet at a virtual, erect, diminished image between $F_1$ and the lens.

Dispersion of white light by a prism. Violet is deviated most, red least; the angular dispersion is $\theta = \delta_V - \delta_R$.

An old brass prism spectroscope: the collimator (with slit) on the right sends a parallel beam to the prism on the central table, and the telescope on the left views the spectrum.
Chromatic aberration. A converging lens brings violet to a focus at $F_V$ and red at $F_R$; the separation $f_R - f_V$ is the longitudinal chromatic aberration.
Spherical aberration. Marginal rays cross the axis at $F_M$, paraxial rays at $F_P$. The narrowest waist between them is the circle of least confusion.

Achromatic doublet: a strong crown-glass convex lens cemented to a weaker flint-glass concave lens. The dispersion of the second cancels that of the first, so red and violet meet at the same focus $F$
Gold-leaf electroscope. Charge given to the disc spreads down the rod to the leaves, which repel each other and diverge; the divergence measures the charge.
A gold-leaf electroscope: the brass disc on top, the rod, and the leaves hanging inside the glass case.
Charging a metal sphere positively by induction with a negatively charged rod. The sphere ends up with a charge opposite to that of the rod, and the rod itself loses nothing.
Coulomb forces are equal, opposite and directed along the line joining the charges — outwards for like charges, inwards for unlike charges.

Flux through a plane area seen edge-on. Only the component $E\cos\theta$ along the normal $\hat{n}$ contributes, so $\Phi_E = EA\cos\theta$.
Field of a uniformly charged conducting sphere of radius $R$. $E = 0$ inside, jumps to $\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ at the surface, then falls as $1/r^2$.
Coaxial cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius $r$ and length $l$ around a line charge $\lambda$. Flux crosses only the curved surface.
For a point charge, $V \propto 1/r$ falls off more slowly than $E \propto 1/r^2$. Both are taken as zero at infinity.
Equipotentials (dashed) and field lines (solid) around a positive point charge. Equal steps of $20\ \text{V}$ lie further and further apart because $V \propto 1/r$.
Uniform field between parallel plates. The equipotentials are flat planes parallel to the plates, and $E = V/d$ is the same everywhere between them.
Equipotential contours of a dipole. The line midway between the charges is the $V = 0$ equipotential, on which no work is done.
Parallel plate capacitor. The field between the plates is uniform, $E = \sigma/\varepsilon_0$, and the potential difference is $V = Ed$.

Charge against potential difference for a capacitor. The gradient is $C$ and the shaded area $\frac{1}{2}QV$ is the stored energy.
A dielectric slab polarized between charged plates. The bound surface charges set up a field $E_p$ opposing $E_0$, so the net field falls to $E_0/\varepsilon_r$.

Taxonomic hierarchy of the human being. The number of organisms in each rank decreases from top to bottom, but their similarity increases.
The five-kingdom classification (Whittaker). Monera is prokaryotic; the other four kingdoms are eukaryotic.
Bacteria seen under a scanning electron microscope: these are rod-shaped bacilli (Escherichia coli). Cocci are round and spirilla are spiral.
Paramecium, a ciliate protist, seen through a microscope. It swims with the help of the cilia that cover its body.
Euglena and other pond-water protists under the microscope. Euglena has a whip-like flagellum for swimming and chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
Amoeba, a protist, seen through a microscope. It moves by extending temporary false feet (pseudopodia).
Penicillium growing on an orange: the green powder is the mass of spores. Penicillium is the fungus that gave us the antibiotic penicillin.
A mushroom (fly agaric), the fruiting body of a fungus. The cap sits on a stalk and the body of the fungus lies in the soil.
Flower of a hibiscus plant. Angiosperms bear flowers, and their seeds are enclosed in fruits.
Moss with its spore capsules (sporophytes) on thin stalks. Mosses are bryophytes: small plants of moist places that have no true roots.
Underside of a fern frond, showing the brown clusters of spore-producing sori. Ferns reproduce by spores, not seeds.
An earthworm (phylum Annelida): the body is divided into many ring-like segments.
A cockroach (phylum Arthropoda): jointed legs, three pairs, and a hard outer skeleton.
Rohu, a fish (class Pisces): the body is covered with scales and it breathes with gills.
A frog (class Amphibia): moist skin, and it lives both in water and on land.
A pigeon (class Aves): a bird has feathers, wings and a beak and is warm-blooded.
The queen (marked with a red dot) among her workers. The queen is longer than the workers and is the only egg-laying female.
Days taken in each stage of development of the queen, the worker and the drone.
Developing honey bees taken from their cells: larvae (white, left) and pupae (right) show the stages between egg and adult.
A frame of comb. The pale capped cells in the middle hold developing brood; workers crowd over the comb.
A beekeeper lifting a frame out of a hive to inspect the comb.
A young pea seedling (Pisum sativum) pushing up through the soil. Mendel grew thousands of such plants and counted their characters.
Flower of the garden pea. Mendel crossed pea plants by moving pollen from the flower of one plant to the flower of another.
Monohybrid cross between pure tall (TT) and pure dwarf (tt) pea plants, giving the F1 and F2 generations.
Dihybrid F2 ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. Each square is one of the 16 boxes in the Punnett square, coloured by phenotype.
The 46 human chromosomes arranged in pairs by size (22 pairs of autosomes) with the sex chromosomes: XY in a male and XX in a female.
Levels of organisation of heredity: from nucleus to chromosome to the DNA double helix with base pairs.
Sex determination in human beings. The sex of the baby is decided by the sperm, not by the egg.
Human chromosomes arranged in pairs (karyotype) of a person with Down syndrome. Chromosome 21 (boxed) has three copies instead of two.
A neuron (nerve cell). Impulses are received by the dendrites, pass through the cell body and travel down the axon to the synapse.
A human brain seen from the left side. The wrinkled outer layer is the cerebrum; the cerebellum lies under its back part.
Reflex arc for withdrawing the hand from a hot object. The impulse reaches the spinal cord and returns without passing through the brain first.
Female reproductive system in its place in the body (front view; the left half shows the inside of the uterus and vagina).
The 28-day menstrual cycle. The uterus lining is shed in days 1 to 5, rebuilds, and keeps thickening after ovulation (day 14); if there is no pregnancy it breaks down again.
A smear of human blood under the microscope. The many pale-red discs are red blood cells; the larger cells with purple nuclei are white blood cells.
A real human heart removed from an adult body, with the large vessels cut short. Compare it with the plan below.
Plan of the human heart showing the four chambers, the main vessels and the direction of blood flow (red: oxygenated, blue: deoxygenated).
A digital blood-pressure monitor on the wrist. It shows the systolic pressure (SYS), the diastolic pressure (DIA) in mm of mercury, and the pulse rate (PUL).
A nephron (schematic): filtration in the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule, reabsorption along the tubule, and urine passing to the collecting duct.
Negative feedback in temperature control. A change from 37 C is detected and corrected so that the temperature returns to normal.
A simple food web of a grassland. Arrows point from the organism that is eaten to the organism that eats it.
Pyramid of energy for the chain grass, grasshopper, frog, snake (values in kJ). Each higher level has only 10 percent of the level below.
Air pollution in Kathmandu: smoke and dust hang over the city and cut down the view.
Solid waste dumped on the bank of the Bagmati river near Kathmandu. Garbage like this pollutes the river water.
Plastic waste choking a roadside drain. Plastic does not rot, so it stays in the soil and blocks water.
The greenhouse effect (schematic). Sunlight passes through the atmosphere; some heat from the Earth is trapped by greenhouse gases and sent back to the surface.
The Khumbu Glacier below Mount Everest in Nepal. Many Himalayan glaciers are shrinking as the climate warms.
Carbon dioxide in the air (annual average, ppm, measured at Mauna Loa, Hawaii) has risen steadily. The values are rounded.
The waste hierarchy. Methods nearer the top are better for the environment.
A landfill site: mixed waste is dumped, compacted and covered with soil. Leachate and methane from it must be managed.

A Bengal tiger in Bardiya National Park, Nepal. National parks protect the habitat of such rare animals.
Greater one-horned rhinoceros with calf in Chitwan National Park, one of the species saved by protection in Nepal.
The snow leopard, the top predator of the high Himalaya, found in Nepal's mountain national parks such as Shey Phoksundo.
Newton's second law. Left: acceleration is proportional to force for a fixed mass. Right: acceleration falls as mass increases for a fixed force of 12 N.
Collision of two trolleys. The total momentum 4 x 6 = 24 kg m/s before the collision is the same as (4 + 2) x 4 = 24 kg m/s after the trolleys stick together.
The Earth rising above the Moon, photographed by the Apollo 8 crew in 1968. The Moon is held in its orbit round the Earth by gravitation.
Variation of g with height above the Earth's surface (R = 6400 km). g falls as 1/(R + h)^2.
A feather lying on the lunar surface after astronaut David Scott dropped it together with a hammer during Apollo 15 (1971). With no air to slow it down, the feather fell as fast as the hammer.
Velocity-time graph for a stone thrown upward at 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s2). It rises for 2 s, stops, then falls back, passing the starting point at 4 s.
Pressure of fresh water increases in a straight line with depth: P = h x 1000 x 9.8 (gauge pressure, atmosphere not included).
A hydraulic bottle jack of the kind used to lift a vehicle. A small force on the handle gives a large lifting force.
A hydraulic press. A small force f on the small piston (area a) gives a large force F on the large piston (area A), because the pressure is the same in the liquid.
A laboratory mercury barometer: the height of the mercury column in the glass tube balances the pressure of the atmosphere.
Sinking, suspended and floating bodies. W is the weight, U the upthrust. A floating body has U = W.
A bimetallic strip. Brass expands more than iron, so on heating the strip bends toward the iron side. At the right, the bending strip breaks a thermostat contact.
Density of water near its freezing point. The density is greatest at 4 degrees C. (Values are approximate and the vertical scale is greatly magnified.)
Heating curve for 0.1 kg of ice at -10 degrees C changed to steam at 100 degrees C. The flat parts are melting and boiling, where heat goes into latent heat and the temperature does not rise.
Section of a thermos flask. The vacuum between the double glass walls stops conduction and convection; the silvered surfaces reduce radiation.
Top: a transverse wave with its crest, trough, amplitude and wavelength. Bottom: a longitudinal wave, where the particles bunch up in compressions (C) and spread out in rarefactions (R).
A set of tuning forks. When a fork is struck its prongs vibrate and produce a sound of one fixed frequency.
Concave mirror: object beyond C. The image forms between F and C and is real, inverted and diminished. (P is the pole, F the focus and C the centre of curvature.)

A step-down transformer on an electricity pole. It lowers the high voltage of the supply line to a safe voltage for houses.
A transformer. Alternating current in the primary coil sets up a changing magnetic flux in the soft iron core; it induces an alternating emf in the secondary coil.
Our Sun, the nearest star, photographed in extreme ultraviolet by NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory. The bright patches are active regions.
Life cycle of stars. A star is born in a nebula; a Sun-like star becomes a red giant and then a white dwarf, while a massive star explodes as a supernova.
Centre of the Milky Way galaxy in infrared light (NASA Spitzer). Our solar system lies in one of its spiral arms.
The Hubble Ultra Deep Field: almost every spot of light is a whole galaxy of billions of stars.
The Sun, the eight planets, the asteroid belt and the Kuiper belt (not to scale for size or distance).
Jupiter, the largest planet, photographed by the Cassini spacecraft. The Great Red Spot is a giant storm.
Saturn and its rings, photographed by the Cassini spacecraft.

The International Space Station orbiting the Earth, with its large solar panels.

RAM (main memory) modules. They plug into the motherboard and hold the programs and data in use.
A hard disk drive with its cover removed. Data are stored on the spinning disc (platter) and read by the arm.
Star, bus and ring network layouts. In a star network every computer connects to a central switch; in a bus, to one shared cable; in a ring, each to its two neighbours.

A wireless router. It connects the computers of a home to the internet by cable and by Wi-Fi.
What happens when you type a web address. The browser asks a DNS server for the IP address, then requests the page from the web server, which sends it back.

Atomic radius (pm): it rises down group 1 (left) and falls across period 3 (right).

Litmus paper strips. Litmus turns red in an acid and blue in a base.
The pH scale with common substances. Each step in pH is a tenfold change in acidity.

Bauxite, the ore from which aluminium is extracted.
Malachite, a green ore of copper (copper carbonate).

Rust on iron: the reddish-brown flaky layer forms when iron is in contact with moist air.
Structural formulas of methane, ethene and ethyne. Carbon forms four bonds in every case: single, double and triple.
Boiling points of the first eight alkanes. The gradual rise with the number of carbon atoms is a property of the homologous series.
Ethanol (ethyl alcohol), a colourless liquid. It is used as a solvent and as a fuel.
Bars of soap. Soap is made by boiling a fat or oil with an alkali such as sodium hydroxide.
Cleaning action of soap. Tails dissolve in the grease droplet; the charged heads point into water, forming a micelle that is washed away.
A tractor spreading chemical fertiliser, such as urea, over a field.
Bags of Portland cement, each holding 25 kg. Cement is mixed with sand and water to make mortar and concrete.
Containers for collecting glass for recycling. Used glass can be melted again and made into new bottles.
Plastic (PET) bottles collected for recycling. Plastics are polymers.
Classification of polymers and plastics.
